paragraphs: Threat intelligence API and MCP server for AI agents and security tooling.
License keys: new sales are temporarily paused while data licensing is finalised. The free tier and x402 remain available.

An autonomous agent acts on things it has never seen before: it pays a wallet, opens a link, installs a package, patches a CVE. PG1 checks that thing first and answers in one machine-readable shape, reasons + status + checks, so the agent can decide on its own and a person can audit why.
features: It never says "safe". PG1 only knows what its sources have recorded, so the best answer it gives is noflags: nothing found in the sources checked. A check that did not finish is unknown, never noflags.

Free to start. The wallet, domain, hostname and package checks are always free. The paid calls start with 5 free calls a day; after that each is 0.01 USD in USDC on Base via x402, with no account or key.

One call before you act: preflightcheck takes the action you are about to take (pay, open, install, patch, trustagent) and its target, runs every relevant check in parallel and returns one decision. It fails closed: a…

Signed results. Every result carries an Ed25519 signature over the request, the result, its sources, a timestamp and PG1's version; check it offline against /.well-known/pg1-signing-key or with the free verifyresult…

The tools that matter most: preflightcheck, checkwalletsanctions, checkwalletage, checkhostnamereputation, checkdomainage, checkpackage, getcvedetails, getcvebatch, getthreatactorprofile and getioccontext.

A "lookalike" verdict means the hostname wasn't directly listed but resembles a known brand domain from the fuzzylist — either a confusable-character/typo skeleton within the stored tolerance (default 3), or a brand keyword (min. 5 chars) embedded alongside other words (e.g. metamask-login.com) — and sets lookalikeof to the matched brand domain; the brand's own real domain and…
These are paid responses, so a source is served only when PG1 may resell it: our own data, public-domain data, or a source whose terms explicitly allow commercial resale.
